v.q: Which exception must be caught or declared with throws?
v.w: SQLException is checked: it is an Exception but not a RuntimeException. The other three are unchecked.

v.q: Which statement about unchecked exceptions is NOT true?
o: The compiler forces callers to catch them
A method need not declare them
v.w: The compiler does not check them. Only checked exceptions force a catch or a throws clause.

v.q: A method has try { return 1; } finally { return 2; }. What does it return?
v.w: The return in finally replaces the one from try. Never return or throw from finally.

v.q: In which case does a finally block NOT run?
o: System.exit is called in the try block
The try block returns a value
The try block throws an exception
A catch block handles the exception
v.w: finally runs after return and after exceptions. It does not run when the JVM exits, crashes, or the try never finishes.

v.q: In what order does try-with-resources close its resources?
o: Only the last one is closed
v.w: Resources are closed from the last opened to the first, so a statement is closed before its connection.

v.q: Which statement about try-with-resources is NOT true?
o: It needs a finally block to close resources
Resources are closed even if the body throws
v.w: The closing is automatic. No finally block is needed.

v.q: The try body throws A and close() throws B. What does the caller receive?
o: A, with B attached as suppressed
Both, wrapped in a new exception
v.w: The body exception stays primary and the close failure is added as suppressed, so the real cause is not hidden.

v.q: Which method reads the exceptions thrown by close() in try-with-resources?
v.w: getSuppressed() returns the exceptions attached to the primary one. getCause() is for chaining.

v.q: Why pass the original exception as the cause when you wrap it?
o: The root cause stays in the stack trace
The caller can catch both types
v.w: The trace then shows Caused by: with the root cause, which is what you need to diagnose the failure.

v.q: Which line keeps the original exception as the cause?
v.w: Pass the exception to the constructor. Copying only the message loses the trace and the type.

o: At the top of a thread, to log and stop
In a constructor, to hide errors
v.w: Only at the very top, to log and shut down cleanly. Elsewhere it hides bugs and errors such as OutOfMemoryError.
Subclasses must come before superclasses. The reverse makes the second block unreachable.

v.q: By default, after which exception does @Transactional commit?
v.w: Spring rolls back for unchecked exceptions and errors, and commits after a checked one unless rollbackFor says otherwise.

v.q: Which setting makes @Transactional roll back for checked exceptions too?
v.w: rollbackFor lists the exception types that must roll the transaction back.

v.q: How should a REST API report a business rule violation?
o: A 4xx ProblemDetail without a stack trace
A 200 response with the stack trace
A 500 response with the SQL text
An HTML page with the class name
v.w: Use a 4xx status with a clear body. Keep the stack trace in the log and never send internals to the client.

v.q: Which logging habit is correct for an exception?
o: Log once, with the exception as an argument
Log and rethrow in every layer
v.w: Log where it is finally handled, with the exception object so the trace and cause chain are printed.
